title: Drug Distribution Imaging of Rabbit Whole-Eye Section by MALDI Mass Spectrometry
author: Naoto Mori
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v7ae9ie

steps.title: Excise and wash eyeball
steps.instruction: Immediately after euthanizing the rabbit, excise the eyeball, wash it in saline to remove ophthalmic solution, and blot excess saline with a paper towel.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze and embed tissue
steps.instruction: Immerse the enucleated eyeball in isopentane cooled with dry ice; if a crack appears, first freeze the eyeball on pulverized dry ice before immersion. Then embed the frozen eyeball in pre‑cooled 2 % (w/v) carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) solution and store the block at –80 °C until sectioning.

steps.title: Mount block and section
steps.instruction: Fix the frozen tissue block on a cryostat stage using optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound (Sakura Finetek, Tokyo, Japan), equilibrate at –20 °C on a Leica CM1950 cryostat, and sagittally cut 10‑µm thick sections. Collect sections onto a 20 Ω indium/tin oxide‑coated glass slide (Matsunami Glass, Osaka, Japan). Replace the razor blade regularly to avoid contamination. If slides are not used immediately, place each slide in a 50 mL tube containing silica gel to prevent condensation, then dry the slides in a desiccator at room temperature before matrix coating.

steps.title: Prepare and spray matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare CHCA matrix at 5 mg mL⁻¹ in 50 % v/v acetonitrile containing 0.1 % v/v trifluoroacetic acid. Using the automated TMSprayer (HTx Technologies, Chapel Hill, NC, USA), spray the matrix onto the tissue sections. Prefer spray coating over vapor deposition to avoid cracks. Optimize matrix compound (e.g., DHB, CHCA, 9‑AA), concentration, solvent, spray speed and flow for each tissue if needed.

steps.title: Optional matrix removal and staining
steps.instruction: If histological staining is required, wash the matrix off the section with 100 % acetone, then stain the tissue with hematoxylin‑eosin (H&E).

steps.title: Acquire optical images
steps.instruction: Scan the slides with an automated NanoZoomer Slide Scanner 2.0‑HT (Hamamatsu Photonics, Shizuoka, Japan) to obtain optical images.

steps.title: Calibrate mass spectrometer
steps.instruction: Calibrate the SolariX FT‑ICR mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonik, Bremen, Germany) equipped with a 7.0‑T superconducting magnet in positive ion mode using sodium formate, following the instrument’s calibration instructions.

steps.title: Set laser and acquire spectra
steps.instruction: Set the laser spot size to medium focus (~50 µm) for low spatial resolution or small focus (~25 µm) for high spatial resolution. Optimize and fix laser intensity at the start of each run, adjusting power on a high‑drug‑concentration region for maximal sensitivity. Set the mass range to m/z 200‑310 (adjust per target compound). Use the CHCA sodium adduct (observed m/z 212.031814) as the lock mass (CHCA proton adduct theoretical m/z 190.05) to maintain mass accuracy, then acquire spectra.
